example.title: WATER TEMPERATURE ON GROWTH AND LIPID METABOLISM IN CHINESE MANDARIN FISH

extract.quote: 在36℃养殖条件下, 雌雄鳜的WGR较28℃和35℃显著降低(P<0.05)。
extract.statement: 在36℃养殖条件下，雌雄鳜的增重率较28℃和35℃显著降低。

map.reason: The claim reports that high temperature (36°C) significantly reduces weight gain rate in mandarin fish compared to lower temperatures. This is a measured result from the study. While it addresses an environmental condition (temperature/water quality) relevant to welfare, the outcome reported is growth (a proxy for welfare/health), not a direct welfare metric like stress hormones or mortality. The reduction in growth indicates a negative impact on the animal's physiological state under that specific condition.

verify.note: WGR即增重率(Weight Gain Rate)，引文与陈述内容一致。

render.text_en: Under rearing conditions at 36°C, the weight gain rate of female and male mandarin fish was significantly lower than at 28°C and 35°C.

name: water temperature regulation
水温调控
cluster.reason: All members concern managing or setting rearing water temperature (high, low, controlled, monitored) for mandarin fish, so they are one practice; only the liver pathology claim C0276 and viral load claim C0422 are not about temperature management itself.

findings.statement_en: In mandarin fish, raising water temperature to 36°C was linked to poorer welfare: growth was strongly inhibited, liver antioxidant enzymes (SOD, CAT) and related gene expression fell, MDA rose in females, and hsp70/hsp90 expression trended down, which the authors read as exceeding the fish's self-protection range. Other claims mostly describe how temperature was set or the ranges used, and one earlier study found higher blood total protein and GOT at 20°C than at other temperatures; background says 25-35°C is the optimal range.
findings.statement_zh: 对鳜来说，把水温升到36°C与福利变差有关：生长受到明显抑制，肝脏抗氧化酶（SOD、CAT）及相关基因表达下降，雌鱼MDA升高，hsp70/hsp90表达总体下降，作者认为这已超出鱼体自身保护范围。其他结论多只是描述控温方式或试验温度范围；另有一项早期研究发现20°C时血清总蛋白和GOT高于其他水温；背景资料称25-35°C为适宜温度范围。

grouping.reason: All members concern managing or setting rearing water temperature (high, low, controlled, monitored) for mandarin fish, so they are one practice; only the liver pathology claim C0276 and viral load claim C0422 are not about temperature management itself.

strength.en: Of 12 claims that take a side: 1 in favour, 11 against or no effect. At least 80% point one way.
strength.zh: 12 条有明确倾向的论断中，1 条支持，11 条反对或无效果，至少 80% 指向同一方向。
strength.rule: one paper; described if more claims describe than take a side; agree or against at 80% or more one way; otherwise mixed

actions.action_en: Avoid holding mandarin fish at water temperatures up to 36°C, and treat temperatures at that level as a welfare risk to be corrected.
actions.action_zh: 养殖者应避免将鳜养殖水温长期保持在高达36°C的水平,并将此类温度视为需要纠正的福利风险。

priority.reason: Seven papers with 18 measured claims show 36°C inhibits growth and weakens antioxidant defences. Avoiding it is a clear step, but the harm threshold between 30°C and 36°C is undefined and cooling costs money.

criteria.note: Heat stress where summer peaks occur
Shading or water exchange, some cost

actions.evidence_gap: The studies tested 36°C in controlled trials, so the temperature at which harm begins between about 30°C and 36°C on commercial farms is not defined.
actions.risks: Cooling or shading to prevent such temperatures adds energy and equipment costs, and the findings do not say what level is a safe upper limit.

basis.reason: Both findings report harm at 36°C: strongly inhibited growth, lower liver antioxidant enzymes, higher liver oxidative damage, and signs of immune fatigue in females. I chose these over the feeding findings because they show a direct harm at high temperature. The harm comes from trials at one extreme temperature, so I limited the action to avoiding that range and did not set a recommended temperature.

findings.why: Growth inhibition and antioxidant and heat-shock changes at 36°C, read as exceeding the fish's self-protection range.
Higher liver oxidative damage and immune fatigue in females at up to 36°C.
